ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 50 V DC power supply, with the positive terminal at the top and the negative terminal at the bottom; the main thyristor Th_M is connected in series in the upper positive bus. On the right side is a constant-current load, labeled load current I_L = 10 A. A 10 µF capacitor is connected at the output node, and the figure indicates that the upper plate of the capacitor is positive and the lower plate is negative. The auxiliary thyristor Th_A is located in the lower branch; according to the connection relationship in the figure, after Th_A is triggered, the lower plate of the capacitor will be clamped to the potential of the power supply positive bus. Reasoning: Taking the negative terminal of the power supply as the reference point, the power supply positive bus is +50 V. The initial capacitor voltage is 50 V, and the upper plate is positive relative to the lower plate. After Th_A is triggered, the lower plate of the capacitor is connected to +50 V, so the potential of the upper plate of the capacitor, that is, the output node, instantaneously becomes 50 V + 50 V = 100 V. At this time, the anode of Th_M is still at +50 V, while the cathode is +100 V, so Th_M obtains reverse bias. The load current is approximately constant at 10 A, which will discharge the 10 µF capacitor. When the capacitor voltage drops from 50 V to 0 V, Th_M no longer remains reverse-biased. Therefore, the available turn-off time is t = C ΔV / I = (10 µF × 50 V) / 10 A = 50 µs. Rounded to the nearest integer is 50.

method.method_draft: After first describing the circuit, assign the source positive bus as +50 V relative to the negative rail. Initially the capacitor has 50 V with the upper plate positive. When Th_A is triggered, use the image topology to set the lower capacitor plate to the source positive bus; therefore the output node/Th_M cathode rises to 50 V + 50 V = 100 V while Th_M anode remains at 50 V, giving reverse bias. The load draws 10 A from the output node, discharging the 10 µF capacitor so its voltage decreases at dv/dt = I_L/C. The available turn-off time is the time for the capacitor voltage to fall from 50 V to 0 V, when the cathode of Th_M is no longer above its anode: t = C(50 V)/10 A = 50 µs.

图像描述：图中左侧是 50 V 直流电源，正端在上、负端在下；上方正母线中串有主晶闸管 Th_M。右侧是恒流负载，标注负载电流 I_L = 10 A。输出节点处接有一个 10 µF 电容，图中标明电容上极板为正、下极板为负。辅助晶闸管 Th_A 位于下方支路，按图中连接关系，触发 Th_A 后会使电容下极板被钳到电源正母线电位。
推理：取电源负端为参考点，则电源正母线为 +50 V。初始电容电压为 50 V，且上极板相对下极板为正。触发 Th_A 后，电容下极板被接到 +50 V，因此电容上极板即输出节点电位瞬时变为 50 V + 50 V = 100 V。此时 Th_M 的阳极仍在 +50 V，而阴极为 +100 V，所以 Th_M 得到反向偏置。负载电流近似恒定为 10 A，会使 10 µF 电容放电，电容电压从 50 V 下降到 0 V 时，Th_M 不再保持反偏。因此可用关断时间为 t = C ΔV / I = (10 µF × 50 V) / 10 A = 50 µs。四舍五入到最近整数为 50。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: When Th_A is triggered, ideal switching clamps the lower capacitor plate to the source positive node. planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses charge balance on the commutating capacitor rather than explicit nodal voltage evolution. It treats the available commutation interval as the time for the load current to remove the initial capacitor charge that is responsible for reverse bias. planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal forced-commutation chopper, the initially stored charge on the commutating capacitor supplies the reverse-bias interval for the main thyristor after the auxiliary thyristor is fired. With constant current, the duration is charge divided by current: t = Q/I, where Q = C V for the voltage swing over which reverse bias exists.
